previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, cough, and shortness of breath two days after potential sick contact. Initial chest X-ray showed subtle right middle lobe changes, prompting empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and azithromycin for possible pneumonia. Nasal swab confirmed RSV infection, and CT scan revealed diffuse bronchial wall thickening and ground-glass opacities consistent with viral bronchiolitis, without focal consolidation. Ceftriaxone was discontinued, and he completed a short course of azithromycin. His blood counts dropped during admission, likely due to RSV or medications, but showed signs of recovery by discharge. He remained stable on room air, with normal oxygen saturation, and returned to his baseline health. He was discharged home with instructions to continue his regular medications, complete azithromycin, use albuterol as needed, and follow up for CBC and INR monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
TYPE OF EXAMINATION:  Chest, PA and lateral.

INDICATION:  Myeloma, cough, and fever, evaluate for infiltrates.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral chest views were obtained with patient in upright
position.  Available for comparison is the next preceding similar study of
___.

The heart size remains within normal limits.  No typical configurational
abnormality is seen.  Mild widening and elongation of the thoracic aorta but
otherwise stable.  The pulmonary vasculature is not congested.  No signs of
acute parenchymal infiltrates are present.  Comparison demonstrates that the
previously described few peripheral linear densities consistent with either
idiopathic fibrosis or COPD remain rather unchanged.  No new acute pulmonary
parenchymal abnormalities are identified.  Previously described skeletal
injury in distal right clavicle and shoulder area is unchanged.  No gross new
skeletal abnormalities are present.

IMPRESSION:  Stable chest findings, no new infiltrates.

PROCEDURE:  CT chest without contrast.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Multiple myeloma, fevers and productive cough.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT chest was performed without IV contrast.  5-mm and 1.25-mm
axial slices were acquired with coronal and sagittal reformats.

COMPARISON:  Previous CT ___.

FINDINGS:  The diffuse bilateral bronchiolitis has worsened in the interval
between the previous CT.  This comprises multiple centrilobular nodules and
linear branching opacities which conform to the peripheral small airways,
with with increased airway thickening which is now moderate and distal
endobronchial mucoid impaction.

Multiple centrilobular nodules are clustered and some are confluent on the
current study; for example, the inferior right upper lobe (4.86), periphery of
the left lower lobe (4.165); and focal areas of consolidation are new, for
example, in the periphery of the left upper lobe (2.22)and in the periphery of
the right upper lobe (2.27). Atelectasis is linear in the right lung base.  No
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes which are 7 mm in the paratracheal region and
8 mm in the aortopulmonary window are stable since the previous study with no
pathological enlargement of mediastinal or axillary lymph nodes by CT size
criteria.

The aorta, pulmonary artery, and heart size is normal with minimal pericardial
effusion most likely physiological.  Central airways are widely patent.

Calcification in the left coronary arteries is moderate. A hiatal hernia is
small. Limited view of the upper abdomen is unremarkable.

No destructive or sclerotic bone lesion. Heterogeneity of the attenuation of
the ribs is unchanged.

IMPRESSION:
1)Increased bronchial airway thickening and bronchiolitis, with centrilobular
nodules which are confluent in areas consistent with active infection.

2)Diffuse coronary artery calcification.
